factor/bowl: Take the simplest loss there is, a bowl: f of x equals a x squared, with its minimum at zero. Here a is one, and x starts at one.
factor/grad: Its gradient is two a x. So one step takes x to x, minus eta times two a x.
factor/factor: Pull out the x, and every step just multiplies x by the same factor: one minus two a eta. With eta at zero point three, that is zero point four.
race/small: With a learning rate of zero point zero five, the factor is zero point nine. Each step keeps ninety percent of x, and the ball creeps.
race/good: With zero point three, the factor is zero point four. x shrinks fast and slides straight in.
race/zig: With zero point eight, the factor is minus zero point six. Each step overshoots to the other side, but lands closer: it zigzags in.
race/big: With one point one, the factor is minus one point two. Every overshoot lands farther out, and training blows up.
limit/line: Plot the factor against eta. It starts at one and falls in a straight line as eta grows.
limit/half: At eta equals one over two a, it is zero: a single step lands right on the minimum.
limit/edge: At one over a, it reaches minus one, and x bounces between two points forever. Any larger, and it blows up.
limit/steep: A steeper bowl, a bigger a, makes the line fall faster. The largest learning rate that does not diverge is one over a.
example/ask: Your turn. The loss is two x squared, x is three, and eta is zero point one. Where is x after one step?
example/grad: The gradient is two a x: two times two times three, twelve.
example/step: The step is zero point one times twelve, one point two. So x goes to three minus one point two: one point eight.
example/check: Check with the factor: one minus two times two times zero point one is zero point six, and zero point six times three is one point eight.
